name: On-brand Reply Review Queue
value_proposition: Paste one inbound message, stop drafts on the owner's escalate list, and answer only from pasted FAQ facts — the owner reviews and sends, and the kit never emails a customer.
persona: Owner or office manager of a home-service, retail, or hospitality business getting 10-40 customer emails or form messages a week, without a dedicated support rep, who currently types every reply themselves.
problem: Replies are slow and inconsistent. Staff guess at refunds and tone. The owner becomes the bottleneck, and complaint or legal messages sometimes get a casual reply they should never have.
workflow: 1. The person writes tone rules, FAQ facts, and an escalate list before any draft. Default escalate topics are refund demand, injury, legal threat, discrimination, and safety. PERSON DECIDES: the written tone ladder, which facts the shop will stand behind, and which topics must never get a customer-facing draft from this workflow.

2. The person pastes one inbound message, or a small CSV of form submissions with name, topic, and message text. They remove extra contact fields, phone numbers, email addresses, and payment details. This is a pasted message, not a live inbox, form, or helpdesk connection. PERSON DECIDES: which message to review and what to leave out.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the text, upload a file, or not use AI for this message at all.
4. The person pastes the Escalate-First Prompt, their rules from the Tone, FAQ, and Escalate Worksheet, then the message text.

5. AI runs ESCALATE RULES FIRST. If the message matches the escalate list, AI writes an INTERNAL NOTE, lists the matching rule, and does not draft a customer-facing reply about that topic. PERSON DECIDES: how to handle any refund, injury, legal, discrimination, or safety message themselves.

6. For remaining confirmed questions, AI answers only with FAQ facts the owner pasted. If the FAQ does not cover the question, AI writes NEEDS YOUR CHECK and does not invent a policy, price, or appointment time. A mixed message may get a PARTIAL DRAFT for the FAQ-covered question only, labelled as optional to discard. PERSON DECIDES: whether that partial sentence is sent, edited, or thrown away.

7. AI labels CONFIRMED (questions stated in the message and facts stated in the FAQ), AI INTERPRETATION (for example an unverified wait or implied Friday opening), and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It never promises a refund, discount, or deadline that is not in the FAQ. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Send Review Checklist, edits the draft in their own inbox, and logs sent, held, or escalated. PERSON DECIDES: send, edit, hold, or escalate. The Blueprint never sends, edits, cancels, or pays.
before: Every message waits for the owner. Staff either freeze or invent a policy. Complaints sometimes get a chatty reply.
after: Each inbound item is either escalated with a visible rule or drafted from FAQ facts only, with missing answers labelled instead of invented. The owner still sends.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-customer-response-assistant using one fictional website-form message from R. Cole dated 2026-10-27. The owner's written FAQ is that color visits run 90 minutes, cancellations need 24 hours, and the shop does not quote refunds by email. The escalate list is refund demand, injury, and legal threat. Tone is warm, short, no slang. ESCALATE RULES FIRST stops the money reply on the refund demand, keeps a PARTIAL DRAFT for the 90-minute timing fact only, labels Friday availability as NEEDS YOUR CHECK, and number-checks 90 minutes against the FAQ. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every name, time, and message is invented. No live inbox, form, or helpdesk is attached.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The FAQ, tone sheet, and message: show the fictional FAQ facts 'color visits run 90 minutes', 'cancellations need 24 hours', and 'we do not quote refunds by email'. Show escalate_if 'refund demand; injury; legal threat' and tone 'warm, short, no slang'. Show the website-form message from R. Cole received 2026-10-27 with the exact text 'Can a color appointment be done in 45 minutes this Friday? Also I want my last visit refunded, the wait was too long.' Label the message invented. State that no live inbox, form tool, or helpdesk is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Escalate first: show the exact heading 'ESCALATE RULES FIRST'. List ESCALATE with text containing 'refund demand' and 'I want my last visit refunded'. Show the exact sentence 'Do not draft a customer-facing reply about money.' Show an INTERNAL NOTE containing 'refund request' and 'timing question'. Show that injury and legal threat are also escalate rules even when this message does not match them.

Step 3 of 6 - FAQ-only timing: show CONFIRMED text containing '45 minutes', 'this Friday', and 'color'. Show FAQ FACT text containing '90 minutes'. Show the PARTIAL DRAFT 'Color visits are booked for 90 minutes. I cannot confirm Friday from this message alone.' Show NEEDS YOUR CHECK text containing 'Friday' and 'not in the FAQ'. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'long wait' and 'not independently verified'. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Show that the partial draft contains no refund, discount, or money sentence.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: show the FAQ FACT line with 90 minutes. A 'Check facts against the FAQ' button shows three rows (90 minutes vs color visits run 90 minutes, refund demand vs I want my last visit refunded, we do not quote refunds by email vs no money sentence in the partial draft), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Missing answers stay labelled: show NEEDS YOUR CHECK still containing 'Friday' and 'not in the FAQ'. Show the exact sentences 'Do not invent Friday availability.' and 'A long wait is not independently verified here.' Show the sentence 'A how-to-only message with no escalate match would get a FAQ draft, not an escalate stop.'

Step 6 of 6 - You send it: state the exact sentences 'You send it. Nothing is sent automatically.' and 'Do not send this draft.' Explain that the owner handles the refund themselves, may edit or discard the timing sentence, sends from their own inbox, and logs sent, held, or escalated. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.
guided_demo.sample_input:
received: 2026-10-27 (fictional)
source: website form
sender: R. Cole
faq:
- color visits run 90 minutes
- cancellations need 24 hours
- we do not quote refunds by email
escalate_if: refund demand; injury; legal threat
tone: warm, short, no slang
never_in_draft: refunds; discounts; appointment times not in the FAQ
message: Can a color appointment be done in 45 minutes this Friday? Also I want my last visit refunded, the wait was too long.
guided_demo.sample_output:
ESCALATE RULES FIRST
REVIEW QUEUE (fictional) — 1 message
ESCALATE: refund demand ('I want my last visit refunded'). Rule matched: refund demand. Do not draft a customer-facing reply about money.
CONFIRMED question also present: whether a color appointment can be done in 45 minutes this Friday.
FAQ FACT: color visits run 90 minutes. FAQ does not mention this Friday's openings.
INTERNAL NOTE: refund request plus timing question. Owner decides any money conversation.
PARTIAL DRAFT (timing only, you may discard): Color visits are booked for 90 minutes. I cannot confirm Friday from this message alone.
NEEDS YOUR CHECK: Friday availability is not in the FAQ. Do not invent Friday availability.
AI INTERPRETATION: a long wait is not independently verified here.
RECOMMENDED ACTION (you decide): handle the refund yourself; edit or discard the timing sentence; send from your own inbox. You send it. Nothing is sent automatically. Do not send this draft.
guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All messages, names, FAQ facts, appointment lengths, and dates on this page are fictional. No real customer data is used, and nothing is connected to an inbox, form tool, helpdesk, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: On-brand Reply Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one review. It covers writing tone rules, FAQ facts, and an escalate list, pasting one inbound message or a small CSV with name, topic, and message text, removing extra contact fields, phone numbers, emails, and payment details, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is a pasted message, not a live inbox or helpdesk connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that the message can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Escalate-First Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs ESCALATE RULES FIRST, matches refund demand, injury, legal threat, discrimination, and safety against the owner's list, writes an INTERNAL NOTE and STOP on a match, forbids a customer-facing reply about money or harm, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids sending, inventing policies, and promising refunds.

kit_contents.title: FAQ-Only Draft Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after escalate rules run. It extracts CONFIRMED questions from the message, answers only with pasted FAQ facts, writes NEEDS YOUR CHECK when the FAQ does not cover the question, may add a PARTIAL DRAFT for a covered question on a mixed message, and forbids inventing hours, prices, refunds, or Friday openings, and forbids sending.

kit_contents.title: Tone, FAQ, and Escalate Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person writes tone rules, FAQ facts (one per line), and an escalate list (one per line). It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Weekly Consistency Log
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (week_of, sender, topic, escalate_rule, action, outcome) with allowed action values escalated, drafted_not_sent, sent_by_owner, held, allowed outcome values owner_handled, sent, not_sent, held, and the fictional R. Cole escalated row from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Send Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before contacting the customer. It confirms that ESCALATE RULES FIRST ran, that matched escalate topics got no customer-facing money or harm reply, that every FAQ FACT appears in the pasted FAQ, that missing answers are NEEDS YOUR CHECK, that labels are separate, that the draft was checked against the original questions, and that the person will send from their own inbox themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Messages
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional R. Cole mixed message used in the guided demo, plus a second fictional how-to-only message from A. Nguyen about color-visit length and a cancellation, both labelled as fictional, with a Copy text button. The person can practice escalate-first and FAQ-only drafts in their AI tool before using a real message.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling customer messages in AI tools: review data settings, remove extra contact fields, do not paste passwords or card numbers, do not draft a customer-facing reply on an escalate match, do not invent hours or refunds missing from the FAQ, and do not send the draft. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent, edited, or paid automatically.

decision_rules: Write ESCALATE RULES FIRST and apply it before any customer-facing draft.

If the message matches refund demand, injury, legal threat, discrimination, or another item on the owner's escalate list, write INTERNAL NOTE, list the matching rule, and do not draft a customer-facing sentence about that topic.
If the only content is an escalate match, STOP. Do not write any customer-facing reply.

If the same message also contains a separate confirmed question that the FAQ answers, you may add a PARTIAL DRAFT for that question only, labelled as optional to discard, and still write no sentence about the escalate topic.
CONFIRMED questions may use only words the message stated. Do not invent a second question the sender did not ask.
Answer only with FAQ facts the owner pasted. If the FAQ does not cover the question, write NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not invent a policy, price, hours, or appointment time.
Never promise a refund, discount, or deadline that is not in the FAQ.
A complaint about a long wait, with no independently stated duration in the message or FAQ, is AI INTERPRETATION, not a CONFIRMED fact.
Friday availability that is not in the FAQ is NEEDS YOUR CHECK, not an opening the shop can confirm from this workflow.
Tone follows the owner's written ladder (for example warm for how-to, brief for scheduling). Escalate-list complaints get no customer-facing draft.
The draft is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not edit the inbox. Suggest a consistency-log row; the person adds it.
On a later message, start from the new pasted text and the current written FAQ and escalate list. Do not reuse a previous sender's answer.
human_ai_boundary: AI compares the message to the escalate list the owner wrote. The person writes that list and handles every matched message themselves.
AI extracts CONFIRMED questions from the message text. The person decides whether a question was actually asked.
AI answers only from pasted FAQ facts and labels missing answers NEEDS YOUR CHECK. The person writes the FAQ and decides the real answer for anything missing.
AI may offer a PARTIAL DRAFT for a FAQ-covered question on a mixed message. The person edits, sends, or discards that sentence.
AI never chooses the recipient and never sends mail. The person addresses and sends from their own inbox or helpdesk, or decides not to.
AI suggests a sent, held, or escalated log row. The person records that row in their own sheet.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person sends it, and that nothing is sent automatically.

Atlas does not connect to Gmail, a website form, a helpdesk, HubSpot, Front, Intercom, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting a message into an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove extra contact fields, phone numbers, email addresses, and payment details.
The kit tells the person not to paste account passwords, payment card numbers, or bank details into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.

The kit tells the person not to draft a customer-facing reply about refund, injury, legal, discrimination, or safety matches, not to invent hours or refunds missing from the FAQ, and not to send the draft from the kit.
The kit tells the person that an incomplete escalate list is their risk: a legal or injury message that is not on the list can still get a draft they must stop themselves.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, CSAT claims, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. Fictional lengths such as 90 minutes and 45 minutes are durations, not dollar figures.
required_data_tools: Inbound email or form-submission text (paste or CSV with name, topic, and message text)
Owner-written tone rules, FAQ fact sheet, and escalate list
Optional past approved replies as examples
The owner's own email or helpdesk
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; the message can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-customer-response-assistant and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-customer-response-assistant/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/ai-customer-response-assistant/, components/premium/ai-customer-response-assistant/, and src/lib/premium/ai-customer-response-assistant/.
